content:
I think this is related to #mathlib4 > GitHub Codespace can't find /etc/localtime

I was trying to come back to the formal-conjectures repo after a while of not contributing and my Lean server keeps crashing. I've tried removing all the containers, images, and volumes on my Docker and pruned the Docker build cache. Still, the issue is persisting.

I'm not sure where else to look? The hash in the image name is always vsc-formal-conjectures-836d095d95751e3c5e95129dd3b5b7c4e88412966e31a0f07d2f13110f11c153-uid:latest which makes me think the image is old? Any help is super appreciated
I think you'll need to be more specific about "keeps crashing". When does it crash? In response to what actions? Can you provide a reproducible setup that others can follow to see the crash?

Oh, sorry! That's my bad for not including more info. It crashes immediately after running lake serve. In the output, it prints the following:

/workspaces/formal-conjectures> lake serve -- /workspaces/formal-conjectures
Watchdog error: no such file or directory (error code: 2)
  file: /etc/localtime
[Error - 12:33:21 AM] The Lean 4 server crashed 1 times in the last 3 minutes. The server will not be restarted. See the output for more information.
[Error - 12:33:21 AM] Server process exited with code 1.

The Lean version is printed just before the error though and it seems to be pretty current so I wouldn't expect to see that bug:

/workspaces/formal-conjectures> lean --version
Lean (version 4.27.0, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, commit db93fe1608548721853390a10cd40580fe7d22ae, Release)

I did do a bit more digging and found that running the Lean version in the image might be a bit out of date? Running docker run --rm [image id] elan toolchain list for me gets leanprover/lean4:v4.11.0-rc2. But the actual container also has v4.27.0 installed.

For a reproducible setup, I ran docker system prune -a --volumes to clean my Docker environment (I started to restart my computer but that might be overkill), opened the formal-conjectures repo in vscode, and clicked on the popup to reopen the folder in a dev container.
Next steps: reproducible setup that can be reduced to a script that you can copy and paste here. :-)

I'll be honest, I'm not entirely sure how to write a script to run the devcontainer steps when vscode does everything for me. It's also probably not worth it since I can just run sudo apt-get install -y tzdata and the error is resolved. I'm still really curious as to why this happened in the first place so I can have that knowledge in my back pocket but it doesn't block me from actually contributing :slight_smile:
(If anyone else figures out whats happening or runs into a similar issue and resolves it, please lmk!!!)
